text:
Parker Kelly went undrafted, came up through Ottawa and has turned into exactly the kind of forward a contender needs. Last week against the Senators he showed both sides of it in one night: a shorthanded goal off the rush, then, as the Denver Gazette's Evan Rawal noted, a turnover in the slot that led to Ottawa's overtime winner.

That's the season in miniature. He has 5 goals and 10 points in 23 games on 13 minutes a night, a step off last season's 21 goals. His 5 goals have come on 2.5 expected, and Colorado has scored 5.3 more than expected with him on the ice, so the finishing is running hot even as the total looks modest. At five on five the Avalanche are about even with him on and a bit worse than when he sits.

His value lives in the details. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 98th percentile among forwards at taking chances away last season, while noting he played with very strong teammates. He blocks shots (22 already) and kills penalties. We'd watch whether the five-on-five numbers recover; that's where his game earns its minutes.
